references.context: Field theory: field automorphism of E, a bijective unital field homomorphism σ:E→E whose inverse is a field homomorphism; fixing a distinguished subfield F elementwise is a separate condition.
references.reason: Field automorphisms are reusable structured isomorphisms, stronger than a bare ring map and distinct from the relative automorphism group Aut(E/F) defined in this formulation.
references.matching_note: Compare the general object-automorphism candidate missing.591b9f9ee5edc9ff8963 without assuming field automorphisms fix F.

references.disposition: The subgroup consists exactly of automorphisms fixing F pointwise, without requiring E/F to be Galois or finite.

references.phrase: minimal polynomial of α over F
factors completely into linear factors over E
references.context: Field and polynomial algebra: polynomial P∈F[T] splits over extension E/F if its image in E[T] is a product c∏_j(T−α_j) of linear factors, including multiplicities, with nonzero scalar c and roots α_j∈E.
references.reason: Complete splitting into degree-one factors is a reusable condition, distinct from the quantification over minimal polynomials defining a normal extension.
references.matching_note: Compare prior candidate missing.447be9a4b8dcf65f4638 and distinguish one root from complete splitting.

references.disposition: Only the minimal polynomials of extension elements are quantified, not every polynomial in F[x].

references.phrase: categories fibred in groupoids X,Y over C

references.context: Category theory: slice (over-)category C/U of a category C over an object U, with objects morphisms V→U and arrows commuting over U; a special ordinary comma-category construction but not the same concept as the general comma category or the existing iso-comma construction.
references.matching_note: The overcategory C/U is the category of all arrows with fixed codomain U and their commuting triangles; no invertibility is assumed and the base object's choice does not create a different prerequisite concept.

references.context: Category fibred in groupoids: a 1-morphism over C, given by a functor C/U→Y commuting with the structure projections to C and compatible with cartesian arrows, considered in the fibred 2-category.
references.reason: Over-base functors are reusable 1-morphism data, different from individual arrows in a fibre and from transformations lying over base identities.
references.matching_note: The slice category C/U was separately assigned a historical missing target in this effective node; retain it. Compare vertical natural-transformation candidates without automatic equivalence.

references.disposition: The universal base-change test must range over every object and such map; a single fibre test is not sufficient.

references.context: Set theory: smallest equivalence relation on Y containing each pair (f(x),g(x)) with x∈X, given by intersection of such equivalence relations or reflexive-symmetric-transitive closure of the prescribed pairs.
references.reason: Generation of an equivalence relation is independently reusable and is more than having an existing equivalence relation or quotient set.
references.matching_note: The quotient topology already received a separate historical classification in this effective node; do not reclassify or duplicate it.

references.context: Point-set topology: quotient (final) topology induced by a surjective continuous map q:X→Q, where U⊆Q is open exactly when q^{-1}(U) is open in X; includes canonical quotient-set maps and the map X→f(X) when equipped with final topology, independently of whether a larger codomain Y is surjected onto.
references.matching_note: Identifies the same final-topology construction induced by a surjection onto its specified target; it is distinct from the set quotient, a subspace topology, an open map condition, or global surjectivity onto an unrelated ambient space.

references.disposition: The relation is generated by all prescribed pairs, not necessarily only those pairs without transitive closure.

references.phrase: open subset U of topological space
references.disposition: An open set U belongs to the existing ambient topology τ already supplied by the topological-space prerequisite. Calling an arbitrary open subset U a variable does not create a new meaning independent of that topology.

references.phrase: closure(U) is open for every open U
references.disposition: The universal quantifier is over all open subsets; it does not say every subset has open closure.
